summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology. I build perception models and take them to deployment: training detection and segmentation networks in PyTorch, then cutting inference latency with TensorRT and hand-written CUDA kernels on Jetson-class hardware. My autonomous driving work in CARLA spans training-data generation through closed-loop validation.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free visual document understanding transformer, for structured field extraction on a custom dataset.
Built preprocessing and GPU training pipelines in PyTorch using the HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder API.
Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% through preprocessing and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for on-device model deployment.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling, achieving +/-8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.
Architected a metal surface inspection perception pipeline combining image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Trained YOLO11n (mAP@50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD lane detection (ResNet-18) with SoftmaxFocalLoss and ParsingRelationLoss; integrated both into an adaptive lane-following control stack.
Generated ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD training frames with zero manual annotation using CARLA semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering.
Validated in Town02 with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions and correct traffic light compliance across multiple laps.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO detection with TensorRT for visual servoing, achieving a 5.2x speedup over eager PyTorch (56.7 -> 10.9 ms, 17.6 -> 92 FPS) on Jetson.
Resolved 11 integration failures including false-positive detections and stale-frame capture; validated 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory, and preallocated buffers.
Cut inference to 49.2 ms from 73.3 ms uncoalesced and 77.5 ms CPU TorchScript, a ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.
